391:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Animal control officer/department means any person(s) agencies designated by the city as a law enforcement officer/agency, for the purposes of issuing citations in relation to their duties under the specifications of this article.
Animal shelter means any facility operated by the city or its authorized agents for the purpose of impounding or caring for animals held under the authority of this article.
Animals, for the purposes of this article, means dog and/or cat.
Circus means a commercial variety show featuring animal acts for public entertainment.
Commercial animal establishment means any pet shop, grooming shop, auction, riding school or stable, zoological park, circus, performing animal exhibition or kennel.
Domestic animal means any animal kept for pleasure rather than utility.
Grooming shop means a commercial establishment where animals are bathed, clipped, plucked or otherwise groomed.
Guard dog means any dog which has been trained to attack persons or other animals independently or upon verbal command. Also, any dog which, while not so trained, is reasonably expected to perform as a guardian of the property upon which he is located.
Kennel means any premises wherein any person engages in the business of boarding, breeding, buying, letting for hire, training for a fee or selling dogs or cats.
Owner means any person, partnership or corporation owning, keeping or harboring one or more animals. An animal shall be deemed to be harbored If it is fed or sheltered for three or more consecutive days.
Performing animal exhibition means any spectacle, display, act or event other than circuses in which performing animals are used.
Pet shop means any person, partnership or corporation, whether operated separately or in conjunction with another business enterprise except for a licensed kennel, that buys, sells, or boards any species of animal.
Public nuisance means any animal which:
(1) Molests passersby or passing vehicles;
(2) Attacks other animals;
(3) Trespasses on school grounds;
(4) Is repeatedly at large;
(5) Damages private or public property; or
(6) Barks, whines or howls in an excessive, continuous or untimely fashion.
Restraint means any animal secured by a leash or lead, no longer than six feet, or inside a fenced area within the real property limits of its owner.
Riding school or stable means any place which has available for hire, boarding and/or riding instruction, any horse, pony, donkey, mule or burro.
Veterinary hospital means any establishment maintained and operated by a licensed veterinarian for surgery, diagnosis and treatment of disease and injury of animals.
Vicious animals means any animal that constitutes a physical threat to human beings or other animals.
Zoological park means any facility, other than a pet shop or kennel, displaying or exhibiting one or more species of nondomesticated animals operated by a person, partnership, corporation or government agency.
(Code 1992, § 10-8-1)

(Code 1992, § 10-8-2; Ord. of 4-7-2009, § 3)
393:
All dogs and cats housed, kept or boarded within the corporate limits of the city shall be inoculated against rabies by a competent veterinarian and a certificate issued to that effect. The owner or any other person responsible for the presence of a dog or cat within the corporate limits shall be liable for the inoculation of the animal and shall provide proof of inoculation for rabies to the city animal control officer upon request.
(Code 1992, § 10-8-3; Ord. of 4-7-2009, § 4)
394:
(a) Any person owning, keeping, harboring or having custody of any dog or cat over four months of age within this municipality must obtain a registration tag as herein provided.
(b) Written application for registration shall be made to a licensed veterinarian who shall include the name and address of the applicant, description of the dog or cat, appropriate fee, and rabies certificate issued by a licensed veterinarian or anti rabies clinic.
(c) Registration for the keeping of dogs or cats shall be for the life of that particular animal, unless revoked or unless ownership changes.
(d) Application for registration must be made within 30 days after obtaining a dog or cat over four months of age, except that this requirement will not apply to the nonresidential keeping of a dog or cat within the city for no longer than 60 days.
(e) Registration fees shall not be required for Seeing Eye Dogs or governmental police dogs.
(f) Upon acceptance of the registration application and fee, the veterinarian shall issue a durable tag stamped with an identifying number and the year of issuance.
(g) Dogs and cats must wear identification tags or collars at all times when off the premises of the owner(s).
(h) The licensing veterinarian shall maintain a record of the identifying numbers of all tags issued and shall make this record available to the public.
(i) No person may use any registration tag for any animal other than the animal for which it was issued.
(Code 1992, § 10-8-4)
395:
(a) All dogs shall be kept under restraint as defined in section 18-191.
(b) Owners shall exercise proper care and control of animals so as to prevent their animals from becoming public nuisances, as defined in section 18-191.
(c) Every female dog or cat in heat shall be confined in a building or secure enclosure in such a manner that such female dog or cat cannot come into contact with another animal except for planned breeding.

In the case of a building, notice shall be conspicuously posted on or about each and every entrance or exit. In the case of a general enclosure in which a guard dog is located, the notices shall be posted upon the enclosure at a distance not greater than 50 feet apart, as well as upon each and every entrance and exit through the enclosure. In the case of apartments, condominiums or businesses located within larger buildings where the guard dog is located solely within the apartment, condominium or business, the notice shall be conspicuously posted on or about each and every entrance and exit to the individual living or business unit.
(Code 1992, § 10-8-5)
396:
It shall be the dog owner's or custodian's responsibility to report all dog bite cases to the county health department.
(Code 1992, § 10-8-6)
397:
(a) Unrestrained dogs and nuisance animals shall be taken by the animal control officers or other duly authorized agents of the city and impounded in the animal shelter and confined in a humane manner.
(b) Impounded dogs and cats shall be kept for not less than seven working days.
(c) If, by a registration tag or other means, the owner of an impounded animal can be identified, the animal control officer shall immediately upon impoundment notify the owner by telephone or mail.
(d) Any owner reclaiming a dog or cat from impoundment shall pay such fees for impoundment, boarding, inoculation and other reasonable fees as may be established by the mayor and council from time to time by appropriate resolution.
(e) Any animal not reclaimed by its owner within seven working days shall become the property of the animal shelter or humane society, and shall be placed for adoption in a suitable home or humanely euthanized.

(g) The owner of an impounded animal may also be proceeded against for violation of this article.

The owner of every animal shall be responsible for the removal of any excretion deposited by his animal(s) on public walks, recreation areas or private property.

Upon a finding by the judge of municipal court that any animal constitutes a public nuisance as defined in section 18-191, the judge may order the owner or custodian to abate the nuisance by permanently removing the animal from the city limits, in addition to other penalties as provided herein. Any person violating any provision of this article shall be punished as provided in section 1-6.

407:
This article shall be known and cited as the "City of Millen Bicycle Helmet Ordinance."
(Code 1992, § 10-9-1)
408:
The city hereby finds and declares that:
(1) Disability and death resulting from injuries sustained in bicycling accidents are a serious threat to the public health, welfare, and safety of the citizens of the city and the prevention of such disability and death is a goal of our community;
(2) Head injuries are the leading cause of disability and death from bicycling accidents; and
(3) The risk of head injury from bicycling accidents is significantly reduced for bicyclists who wear proper protective bicycle helmets.
(Code 1992, § 10-9-2)
409:
As used in this article, the following terms have the following meaning unless the context clearly requires otherwise:
Operator means any person seated on a saddle seat from which that person is intended to and can pedal the bicycle.
Passenger means any person who travels on a bicycle in any manner except as an operator.
Protective bicycle helmet means a piece of headgear which meets or exceeds the impact standards for protective bicycle helmets set by the American National Standards Institute (ANSI) or the Snell Memorial Foundation, or which is otherwise approved by the director of public safety.
Public bicycle path means a right-of-way under the jurisdiction of the state or city for use primarily by bicycles and pedestrians.
(Code 1992, § 10-9-3)
410:
(a) No person under the age of 18 years shall operate or be a passenger on a bicycle on a public roadway, sidewalk, or public bicycle path unless at all times when the person is so engaged he or she wears a protective bicycle helmet of good fit fastened securely upon the head with the straps of the helmet.
(b) No person shall rent, lease, or loan a bicycle for the use of another person under the age of 18 years unless that other person is in possession of a protective bicycle helmet of good fit at the time of such rental, lease, or loan.
(Code 1992, § 10-9-4)
411:
(a) A violation of this article is a civil infraction punishable by a fine of not more than $50.00.
(b) Any public safety officer observing a person operating or being a passenger upon a bicycle without wearing a protective bicycle helmet and reasonably believing the person to be under 18 years of age may stop and temporarily detain such person for purposes of establishing identity and issuing an appropriate warning or citation.
(Code 1992, § 10-9-5)

(Code 1992, § 10-10-1)
